gen_risks.description: The newly created Project Implementation Unit (PIU) lacks experience with World Bank‑financed projects, risking weak fiduciary and compliance controls.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement intensive capacity‑building on World Bank FM, procurement and ESG procedures; assign senior technical advisors and conduct regular audits.
gen_risks.evidence: III.A: GORE has experience ... but does not have experience implementing WB‑financed projects, so capacity building will be required.

gen_risks.description: Delayed recruitment of key financial management and technical staff could postpone project start‑up and disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare detailed TORs early, launch recruitment within 30 days of effectiveness, and use interim consultants to cover gaps.
gen_risks.evidence: B. FM risk: Delayed recruitment of FM staff; terms of reference will be prepared and staff appointed within two months.

gen_risks.description: Budget allocation and execution delays, common in Peru, may slow implementation and affect cash flow.
gen_risks.mitigation: Begin budget allocation process immediately after loan signing; set internal milestones and monitor execution monthly against the Project Operations Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: B. FM risk: Budget allocation and execution delays are typical in Peru’s initial project phases.

gen_risks.description: Inaccurate accounting or financial reporting due to limited experience with Bank‑financed projects could trigger audit findings and repayment issues.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt the national accounting system (SIAF), conduct annual independent audits, and provide staff training on WB reporting standards.
gen_risks.evidence: B. FM risk: Potential inaccuracies in accounting and financial reporting due to inadequate experience.

gen_risks.description: Fragmented institutional landscape and weak inter‑agency coordination may cause project delays and cost overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Activate the high‑level Steering and Consultative Committees, formalize Interinstitutional Agreements early, and use a coordination matrix to track responsibilities.
gen_risks.evidence: B. Sectoral and Institutional Context: lack of coordination within a highly fragmented institutional landscape.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related hazards (floods, landslides, earthquakes) could damage upgraded roads and heritage sites, undermining project benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate‑resilient design standards (drainage, slope stabilization, seismic retrofitting) and conduct regular hazard monitoring during construction and operation.
gen_risks.evidence: 11: Climate hazards ... floods, landslides, droughts ... affect the tourism sector.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient road safety features may lead to high accident rates, deterring tourists and increasing fatalities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement comprehensive safety designs (guardrails, signage, pedestrian crossings) and conduct road safety audits before commissioning.
gen_risks.evidence: 36: Arequipa has a higher road fatality rate; designs will include safety features.

gen_risks.description: Poor water and sanitation infrastructure could create health hazards for visitors and locals, reducing tourism attractiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade water supply, sewage and wastewater treatment to meet health standards; establish O&M plans and regular water quality monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: 10: Poor water and sanitation facilities create a health hazard for communities and tourists.

gen_risks.description: Sexual exploitation and harassment (SEA/SH) risks may deter women’s participation and generate reputational damage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce the SEA/SH Action Plan, provide training on gender‑sensitive conduct, and set up a confidential grievance mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: 21: Project’s action plan on SEA and SH will address barriers to entry.

gen_risks.description: Existing gender wage and participation gaps could limit women’s benefit from tourism jobs, undermining inclusion goals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Target capacity‑building for women’s associations, monitor gender employment indicators, and promote women‑owned enterprises through procurement preferences.
gen_risks.evidence: 20: Gender gap in labor force participation; women face wage gaps and barriers.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private sector investment may leave the project’s demand generation and sustainability objectives unmet.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a clear investment pipeline, use the Obras por Impuestos mechanism, and provide investment incentives (tax breaks, PPP models).
gen_risks.evidence: 23: Private sector willing to invest once infrastructure is upgraded; examples of PPP and Obras por Impuestos.

gen_risks.description: Procurement staff’s limited familiarity with World Bank procurement rules could cause non‑compliance and delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted procurement training, use standard WB procurement documents, and conduct pre‑bid reviews by the Bank’s procurement specialists.
gen_risks.evidence: 63: Project procurement will follow World Bank’s Procurement Regulations; GORE’s logistics office responsible.

gen_risks.description: Disbursement is conditional on signing three Interinstitutional Agreements; delays in these could stall cash flow.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize negotiation and signing of Interinstitutional Agreements within the first 60 days; monitor progress weekly.
gen_risks.evidence: Conditions: No withdrawals shall be made ... unless at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate data collection and monitoring may prevent accurate assessment of project outcomes and trigger performance penalties.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish the tourism information system early, train PIU staff on data protocols, and conduct periodic data quality audits.
gen_risks.evidence: 22: Stakeholder Engagement Plan includes indicators; data collection will require complementary mechanisms by the PIU.

gen_risks.description: Tourism demand may fall short of forecasts, reducing economic returns and job creation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement aggressive marketing (Component 3), diversify tourism products, and monitor demand trends to adjust promotion strategies promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: 53: Sensitivity analysis shows NPV drops with 25% shock to tourism consumption.

gen_risks.description: Future pandemics or health crises could sharply reduce tourist arrivals, affecting revenue projections.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop health‑security protocols for tourism sites, promote domestic tourism, and maintain flexible marketing plans to shift target markets quickly.
gen_risks.evidence: 3: Pandemic severely impacted the sector; 2025 arrivals at 78% of pre‑pandemic levels.

gen_risks.description: Political instability may disrupt government support, funding flows, or policy continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure multi‑year commitments from MINCETUR and MEF, embed project governance in legal agreements, and maintain regular dialogue with political leaders.
gen_risks.evidence: 1: Recent years show increased political instability.

gen_risks.description: Cost overruns due to fragmented responsibilities and unforeseen technical challenges could exhaust the financing envelope.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement rigorous cost monitoring, contingency budgeting (5% of component costs), and require periodic financial reporting to the Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: 42: Coordination across ministries and sectors is complex; lack of strategic national investment plan.

gen_risks.description: Community grievances not addressed timely may lead to social opposition and project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Activate the grievance redress mechanism, set a 30‑day response target, and publish quarterly grievance resolution reports.
gen_risks.evidence: 22: Indicator on percentage of project‑related grievances addressed by the PIU.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient climate‑resilience of water and sanitation infrastructure could lead to service disruptions during extreme events.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design water and wastewater systems with flood‑resilient components, conduct climate risk assessments, and establish emergency O&M protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: 38: Subcomponent 2.2 promotes resilience against floods by providing sewage systems.

gt_risks.description: Peru is in a period of substantial political uncertainty (low popular support for the executive and Congress, high political fragmentation); a new government assumes office July 2026 and regional elections are scheduled October 2026. Since GORE Arequipa (a regional government) is the implementing agency, regional government changes could slow implementation or shift priorities; high-level changes at MINCETUR could also affect oversight commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Focus on highly needed, consensus-driven investments; maintain buy-in and continuous dialogue with the tourism private sector; engage proactively with any new authorities on project opportunities; use implementation arrangements that are technically strong, highly competent, and relatively shielded from political influence and staff turnover.

gt_risks.description: Tourism projects are inherently complex, involving infrastructure, capacity building, and multiple government levels/sectors plus private-sector and community stakeholders. Capacity must be built at GORE Arequipa given no precedent for multisectoral regional investment programs in Peru, and historic national-regional coordination weaknesses. The project also does not budget for O&M of delivered sites/infrastructure, which falls to designated stakeholders.
gt_risks.mitigation: Institutional capacity building via the Project (incl. GFPP) to ready GORE for implementation; World Bank support on PIU composition and key staff selection; coordination arrangements/agreements between the PIU and local partners in charge of operating sites, to align on design, implementation, and handover.

gt_risks.description: Combined fiduciary risk with GORE Arequipa is Substantial, reflecting the entity's lack of prior experience with World Bank or other MDB-financed operations in both financial management and procurement.
gt_risks.mitigation: A fiduciary assessment identified capacity gaps and informed mitigation measures; recruit dedicated FM and Procurement Specialists supported by qualified administrative staff; detail minimum FM/procurement procedures aligned with WB requirements in the Project Operational Manual; use SIAF for financial transactions/reporting and STEP for procurement planning/monitoring; targeted WB training, regular fiduciary supervision, and annual audits.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk reflects the scope/nature of planned interventions, works located in environmentally and culturally sensitive areas, and GORE Arequipa's limited institutional capacity to manage risks per the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthen PIU capacity to manage E&S risks with adequate resources/staffing; elaborate and implement project-level instruments (Stakeholder Engagement Plan, Labor Management Plan, SEA/SH Plan) plus intervention-level instruments with specific mitigation measures.
